title: Event bus core in Java
idea: The event bus core queues each event per subscriber, then dispatches in passes: retrying failures, holding later events of a failed key, dead-lettering at the limit.

analogy.text: A courier serves one office per round. If desk 4 refuses a parcel, desk 4's later parcels wait for the next round; other desks still get theirs.
analogy.breaks: A real courier would not hold parcels back to keep their order.

points: Publish only enqueues: one `Delivery` per matching subscription, in publish order.
A handler that returns acknowledges; a handler that throws asks for a retry.
After one failure, later events with that key wait for the next pass.
At the attempt limit the event moves to dead letters and the key unblocks.

steps.caption: Four events were published. Billing's mailbox holds one delivery for each, in publish order.
Pass 1: billing throws on EV-1. It moves to the retry list, and key O-1 is now blocked.
EV-2 shares key O-1, so it is held without calling the handler. O-1 keeps its order.
EV-3 has key O-2, which is not blocked, so it is handled right away.
EV-4 fails its first try and joins the retry list.
End of pass 1: the retry list becomes the mailbox again, in the same order.
Pass 2: EV-1 succeeds, so EV-2 follows it. EV-4 fails a second time.
Pass 3: EV-4 fails its third try. With a limit of three, it moves to dead letters.

code.title: Retries and dead letters
code.caption: A complete single-threaded core. Topic is shortened to a list and unsubscribe is left out; both work as on the previous page.

walk.text: At most three attempts. Billing fails EV-1 once and EV-4 always.
Run passes until nothing is pending, then list the dead letters.
Publish only enqueues one Delivery per matching subscription: the fan-out.
Each pass tracks keys that failed and collects deliveries for later.
A delivery whose key is blocked is held without a call, keeping per-key order.
Count the attempt. On failure retry next pass, or dead-letter at the limit.
Held and failed deliveries return to the mailbox in their original order.

pitfalls: Never retry a failed event at the back while later same-key events run first.
Keep each subscriber's mailbox separate, so one failing handler never stalls the others.
Store the full event, error and attempt count, so someone can diagnose and replay it.

quiz.q: What is billing's first line in pass 2?
quiz.why: The retry list keeps original order, EV-1 then EV-2 then EV-4. A new pass starts with an empty blocked set, so EV-1 runs first and succeeds.

takeaway: Enqueue per subscriber, retry in order per key, and dead-letter at the limit.

starters: Why does a dead-lettered event unblock its key?
How would I add a delay between retry passes?
What changes if order must hold across all keys, not per key?
